open_points.subject: HTTP route catalog after removal of email-challenge operations
open_points.text: A10 says the portal has “no email verification, no email change confirmed at a new address, no password-reset token” and State 0 R0-15 says it “has no email-challenge or password-reset operation”; State 1 reduces request bodies from 26 to “20 in all since the removal,” but State 2 still carries `rules.http_router_backend` as “(56 routes, Factory `300bd11d` … `a6916180314d`)” without removing or recounting its former challenge routes.
open_points.question: Must the six former email-verification, email-change, and password-reset HTTP operations be absent from the router, with the route catalog and count reduced, or must the accepted 56-route backend retain them as inert endpoints?
options: Remove the six former operations from the router and recompute the route count.
Retain the former inert endpoints so the router still has 56 routes.
open_points.default_guess: Remove all six former challenge operations from the router and recompute the count.

witness.initial: The service is assembled from the carried HTTP router backend after the 2026-11-07 removal.
events: An unauthenticated caller sends a request to the former password-reset-request path.
outcomes: No route exists, so routing returns the ordinary route-not-found response.
The retained inert route accepts the request, returns its concealed response, and changes nothing.
witness.observer: The API caller sees a different HTTP status and response.
